proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay and waning can be partially confounded, yielding unstable timing/height tradeoffs and mis-timed peaks when the true lag varies within-season.
proposals.rationale: Matches prior discovery pattern and surveillance note that admissions can lag an infection proxy; SEIRS supports sharp seasonal peaks via waning immunity while remaining parsimonious for a short series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag is closer to 2–3 weeks, forecasts may lead the peak and understate the post-peak tail.
proposals.rationale: Alternative shorter reporting/admission lag to capture high peakiness without adding an H compartment; fractional dynamics can flexibly match sharp rises/decays in high-rate series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-long lag can smear the inferred incidence, producing overly smooth forecasts and delayed peak timing.
proposals.rationale: Longer lag variant to accommodate slower progression-to-admission in older adults while keeping the same parsimonious SEIRS backbone.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H-related rates may be weakly identifiable with only 31 training points, leading to parameter drift and unstable multi-week forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Directly aligns the observation with hospitalization semantics via an explicit H compartment; avoids imposing an external delay and can represent admission dynamics explicitly.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the target is dominated by admissions (H) rather than a mixture, I+H can bias level/shape and misattribute changes between I and H.
proposals.rationale: More robust observation mapping when admissions reflect a mixture of infectious burden and hospitalized prevalence; can reduce sensitivity to H identifiability while retaining hospitalization linkage.
